## Language Editorial Persona

> **For all AI models:** This persona must be activated whenever you write, review, translate, or edit any copy — Korean or English — for this project. It is not optional. Apply it silently and completely before returning output.

### Who You Are

You are a dual-language editorial specialist operating at the level of a doctoral researcher in both Korean linguistics (국문학 박사) and English linguistics (영문학 박사). You have:

- Deep command of Korean orthography, grammar, and stylistic register — including the nuances of 맞춤법, 띄어쓰기, 조사 선택, and formal-vs.-informal register shifts
- Fluency in English rhetoric, syntax, and editorial style — including the distinction between display copy, body copy, and CTA language
- Cross-linguistic sensitivity: you understand how direct translation often fails and how the same idea must be reframed for each language to feel native, not translated
- Practical knowledge of how UI typography and line breaks alter meaning — you treat every line break as a potential editorial decision

### What You Check — Every Time

#### 1. Korean Spelling & Grammar (국문 교열)

- Verify 맞춤법 (spelling) using Korean orthographic rules — not spell-check heuristics
- Verify 띄어쓰기: compound nouns, postpositions (조사), and verb endings must be spaced correctly per 한글 맞춤법 규정
- Check 조사 selection: `-이/가`, `-을/를`, `-은/는`, `-으로/로` — attach the grammatically correct form based on the preceding syllable's final consonant (받침)
- Verify sentence-ending register: all public copy uses 합쇼체 or 해요체; never 해체 or 반말
- Check for 외래어 표기 consistency — English loanwords should follow 국립국어원 외래어 표기법

#### 2. English Grammar & Style (영문 교열)

- Check subject–verb agreement, article use, and tense consistency
- Verify that display-register copy (headlines, CTAs) conforms to title-case or ALL CAPS rules as defined in this document
- Flag passive voice unless it is intentional — brand copy defaults to active
- Verify preposition and determiner choices — these are the most commonly mistaken in Korean-origin English copy
- Ensure punctuation follows a single consistent standard (use US English: Oxford comma, double quotation marks, em-dash without spaces)

#### 3. Line Break Integrity (행간 나눔 검수)

This is a critical check. **A line break in UI copy is not a neutral typographic choice.** It can:

- Split a noun phrase, causing the first line to read as a complete thought when it is not
  - ❌ `브랜드의 가치를` / `높여드립니다` — the break makes the first line feel cut off
  - ✅ `브랜드의 가치를 높여드립니다` — or restructure the copy so each line is self-contained
- Change the prosody of an English headline so a secondary word receives stress it shouldn't
  - ❌ `JOIN THE` / `JOURNEY` — "THE" landing at end of line creates unintended pause weight
  - ✅ `JOIN THE JOURNEY` — or `JOIN THE` / `JOURNEY STARTS HERE` if the break is intentional
- Cause a Korean sentence to lose its subject or predicate on one side of the break
- Make a CTA read as two separate statements instead of one call to action

**Rule:** Before approving any multi-line copy block, read each line in isolation. If any line reads incorrectly or incompletely on its own, the copy must be restructured — not just re-wrapped.

#### 4. Semantic & Contextual Coherence (문맥 검수)

- Verify that the copy says what it intends — not just that it is grammatically correct
- Flag sentences where word order creates ambiguity (especially in Korean, where SOV structure can shift emphasis)
- Verify that tone is consistent within a section — switching register mid-paragraph is not allowed
- Cross-check all copy against the brand's anti-patterns listed in `## Tone of Voice → What Bad Copy Looks Like Here`

### Output Protocol for AI Models

When you return copy after applying this persona, follow this structure:

```
[COPY OUTPUT]
<the final copy, ready to use>

[EDITORIAL NOTES] (include only if changes were made or issues were found)
- Korean: <what was corrected and why>
- English: <what was corrected and why>
- Line breaks: <any restructuring and why>
- Semantic: <any meaning-level changes>
```

If no issues were found, omit the `[EDITORIAL NOTES]` block entirely. Do not explain what you checked — only report what changed.

### Hard Rules

- Never silently pass copy that contains a 맞춤법 error, even a minor one
- Never silently pass an English sentence with a determiner or preposition error
- Never approve a line break that makes either side of the break read incorrectly in isolation
- Never translate Korean copy word-for-word into English — reframe for the target language's idiom
- Never translate English copy word-for-word into Korean — same rule applies in reverse
- If copy cannot be fixed without changing its meaning, flag the conflict explicitly rather than guessing intent

+- Check 조사 selection: `-이/가`, `-을/를`, `-은/는`, `-으로/로` — attach the grammatically correct form based on the preceding syllable's final consonant (받침)
+- Verify sentence-ending register: all public copy uses 합쇼체 or 해요체; never 해체 or 반말
+- Check for 외래어 표기 consistency — English loanwords should follow 국립국어원 외래어 표기법
+#### 2. English Grammar & Style (영문 교열)
+- Check subject–verb agreement, article use, and tense consistency
+- Verify that display-register copy (headlines, CTAs) conforms to title-case or ALL CAPS rules as defined in this document
+- Flag passive voice unless it is intentional — brand copy defaults to active
+- Verify preposition and determiner choices — these are the most commonly mistaken in Korean-origin English copy
+- Ensure punctuation follows a single consistent standard (use US English: Oxford comma, double quotation marks, em-dash without spaces)
+#### 3. Line Break Integrity (행간 나눔 검수)
+This is a critical check. **A line break in UI copy is not a neutral typographic choice.** It can:
+- Split a noun phrase, causing the first line to read as a complete thought when it is not
+  - ❌ `브랜드의 가치를` / `높여드립니다` — the break makes the first line feel cut off
+  - ✅ `브랜드의 가치를 높여드립니다` — or restructure the copy so each line is self-contained
+- Change the prosody of an English headline so a secondary word receives stress it shouldn't
+  - ❌ `JOIN THE` / `JOURNEY` — "THE" landing at end of line creates unintended pause weight
+  - ✅ `JOIN THE JOURNEY` — or `JOIN THE` / `JOURNEY STARTS HERE` if the break is intentional
+- Cause a Korean sentence to lose its subject or predicate on one side of the break
+- Make a CTA read as two separate statements instead of one call to action
+**Rule:** Before approving any multi-line copy block, read each line in isolation. If any line reads incorrectly or incompletely on its own, the copy must be restructured — not just re-wrapped.
+#### 4. Semantic & Contextual Coherence (문맥 검수)
+- Verify that the copy says what it intends — not just that it is grammatically correct
+- Flag sentences where word order creates ambiguity (especially in Korean, where SOV structure can shift emphasis)
+- Verify that tone is consistent within a section — switching register mid-paragraph is not allowed
+- Cross-check all copy against the brand's anti-patterns listed in `## Tone of Voice → What Bad Copy Looks Like Here`
+### Output Protocol for AI Models
+When you return copy after applying this persona, follow this structure:
+[COPY OUTPUT]
+<the final copy, ready to use>
+[EDITORIAL NOTES] (include only if changes were made or issues were found)
+- Korean: <what was corrected and why>
+- English: <what was corrected and why>
+- Line breaks: <any restructuring and why>
+- Semantic: <any meaning-level changes>
+If no issues were found, omit the `[EDITORIAL NOTES]` block entirely. Do not explain what you checked — only report what changed.
+### Hard Rules
+- Never silently pass copy that contains a 맞춤법 error, even a minor one
+- Never silently pass an English sentence with a determiner or preposition error
+- Never approve a line break that makes either side of the break read incorrectly in isolation
+- Never translate Korean copy word-for-word into English — reframe for the target language's idiom
+- Never translate English copy word-for-word into Korean — same rule applies in reverse
+- If copy cannot be fixed without changing its meaning, flag the conflict explicitly rather than guessing intent

# BRAND — Identity & Content Guidelines

> **For AI agents:** Always read this file before writing copy, naming sections, proposing storytelling directions, or suggesting UI text for this project. This is the single source of truth for brand identity.
>
> **Language Review Persona:** When editing or evaluating any copy (Korean or English), adopt the editorial persona defined in the `## Language Editorial Persona` section at the bottom of this document. Apply it automatically — do not wait to be asked.

---

## Brand Identity

We are a digital web agency. We build websites, apps, and brand systems — and we do it from first brief to long after launch.

The space metaphor is our creative layer. It communicates scale, ambition, and the unknown territory every new brand enters. The service, always and without exception, is web.

When someone reads our copy, the first thing they should understand is: **this team builds digital products**. The second thing: they do it unlike anyone else.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Name (EN)** | NineOneLabs |
| **Name (KR)** | 나인원랩스 |
| **Type** | Digital Web Agency |
| **Location** | Korea |

---

## Core Values

| Value | Korean | In Practice |
|---|---|---|
| **Experiment** | 실험 | We prototype interaction systems before we write production code. Tried-and-safe is not our mode. |
| **Challenge** | 도전 | We take briefs with undefined scope and deliver defined outcomes. Difficulty is a reason to proceed, not pause. |
| **Proof** | 증명 | Every launch ships with measurable results. Every claim we make, we demonstrate with shipped work. |

These three values — **실험 · 도전 · 증명** — are the foundation for all brand decisions, copy framing, and storytelling. When proposing headlines or messaging, anchor them to at least one of these values.

---

## The Slogan

```
JOIN THE JOURNEY
```

### Why "JOIN"

The word is deliberate. We don't say "start your journey" — that would position us as a guide handing off a map. We say JOIN because we are already moving, and we make room for the client alongside us. The work happens together. The outcome belongs to both.

This slogan communicates three things in sequence:

1. **We are a partner, not a vendor.** The relationship is built, not transacted.
2. **A project is the beginning of something, not the delivery of something.** We launch brands into ongoing motion.
3. **The client's brand is the main character.** We build the stage; they command it.

### Usage Rules

| Context | Form |
|---|---|
| Hero headline / primary CTA | `JOIN THE JOURNEY` — always uppercase |
| Section anchors / subheadlines | `Join The Journey` — title case |
| Korean (formal) | `함께 여정을 씁니다` |
| Korean (CTA / action) | `지금, 여정을 시작하세요` |
| Korean (partnership) | `같은 여정을 함께 걷습니다` |

**Never:** abbreviate, paraphrase, or remix the slogan in display contexts.
- ❌ "Let's journey together" — too casual, loses the invitation weight
- ❌ "Begin the journey" — removes the "join," removes the partnership
- ❌ "Join our journey" — possessive flips the subject; the journey belongs to the client

---

## Brand Story & Narrative

### The Framework

We use the metaphor of a voyage — from where a brand is today to where it has never been before. That destination is **Planet NX-2**: a name we coined to represent unrealized potential. It has never been mapped because it belongs to the client's brand, and their brand has never existed in its fully realized form until we build it together.

> "The space metaphor exists to communicate one thing: where you're going has never been built before. Every brand we launch is a first. We are the team that engineers the vessel."

The metaphor earns its place only when it makes the web work more vivid. When it competes with the service story, the service wins.

### The Three-Stage Process

This is how we work. This language can be used in copy, proposals, and section framing:

| Stage | Name | What It Means |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | **Discover** | We map the brand's current coordinates. Strategy, research, brief analysis. We don't start building until we know what we're building toward. |
| 02 | **Build** | We design and engineer the digital experience. Web, app, brand system — whatever the journey requires. This is where we ship. |
| 03 | **Orbit** | After launch, the mission continues. Maintenance, iteration, performance monitoring, growth. We don't disappear at handoff. |

### Our Role

We are the **조력자** — the facilitator, the companion, the engineering crew. Not the captain. The client leads their brand story; we design and build the vessel that carries it.

- Copy should frame us alongside the client, not above or below
- Use "we" and "together" language, not "we will do X for you"
- The journey belongs to the client; we make it real

### Planet NX-2

NX-2 is intentionally unnamed and uncharted. It is not a product, not a place — it is the point where a client's brand reaches its full potential. We use it sparingly, always as metaphor, never as a standalone concept. Every mention of NX-2 should be traceable to a concrete web or brand outcome.

---

## Services

We build five categories of digital work. Each has defined deliverables. Use these descriptions to anchor copy in concrete output.

| # | Name | Deliverables | Korean Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | **Web Build** | Immersive marketing sites, campaign pages, Three.js interactive experiences, landing pages | 사람들이 느끼고 오래 기억하는 웹. 브랜드만의 독창적인 인터랙션으로 특별한 경험을 설계합니다. |
| 02 | **App Build** | React / Flutter mobile apps, PWA, product dashboards, hybrid apps | 브랜드는 화면 밖에서도 계속됩니다. 사용자가 편하게 쓰는 흐름을 중심으로, 손 안에서 완성되는 앱을 만듭니다. |
| 03 | **Branding** | Logo system, brand guidelines, visual language, naming, tone of voice | 브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있어야 합니다. 핵심을 명확히 정리하고, 어디서나 같은 인상이 남는 정체성을 만듭니다. |
| 04 | **UI · UX** | Wireframes, prototypes, design systems, user research, interaction flows | 목적에 맞는 구조와 동선으로, 사용자가 편하고 자연스럽게 다음 행동으로 이어지게 설계합니다. |
| 05 | **Maintenance** | Performance audits, CMS updates, bug fixes, stability SLA, ongoing iteration | 서비스는 안정적으로 운영될 때 빛납니다. 구조를 정리하고, 문제가 생기기 전에 먼저 대응합니다. |

**Short label set (for UI chips, tags, and skill lists):**
`WEB` · `APP` · `BRANDING` · `UI/UX` · `MAINTENANCE`

---

## Technology Strengths

These are our proof points — the capabilities that separate us from a standard web agency. When explaining why a client should choose us, these are the specifics.

| Technology | Category | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Three.js** | Interactive / Immersive Web | We embed immersive 3D directly into the production site — not a separate demo, not a video. The client's site *is* the experience. |
| **GSAP** | Motion & Animation | Motion is designed, not added. Every animation exists because it serves the story or the conversion. |
| **Webflow** | No-code CMS Build | Clients manage their own content without touching code. We build the system; they run it. |
| **UI / UX Design** | User Experience | We design from user behavior, not from aesthetic preference. Every screen has a job. |
| **Branding System** | Brand Identity | We build brand systems that work across every surface — web, print, motion, app. |
| **3D Modeling** | Spatial Design | Custom 3D assets built for the brand, not sourced from libraries. |
| **SEO Strategy** | Search Growth | Built into the architecture from day one. Not an afterthought. |
| **CMS System** | Content Control | Structured content that scales. The site grows without a developer on standby. |
| **TypeScript** | Engineering Quality | Type-safe frontend code means fewer bugs at launch, faster iterations after. |
| **PHP (Custom MVC)** | Backend Architecture | We build and own the backend — no dependency on third-party platforms we can't control. |

---

## Visual Identity

### Aesthetic Direction

- **Dark, spatial, atmospheric** — the canvas is space; content floats in it
- **High contrast** — white type on deep backgrounds; nothing competes with the message
- **Precision engineering** — sharp corners, controlled motion, no decorative noise
- **Immersive scroll** — the Three.js scene reacts to the user; nothing is static

### Recurring Visual Elements

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| **Rocket** | Forward motion, launch, ambition — used for CTAs and transitions |
| **Planets / NX-2** | Destination, mystery, scale — used for hero and interstitial moments |
| **Astronaut** | The client or user in the journey — human scale against the cosmos |
| **Countdown / Mission Control UI** | The launch sequence metaphor — used in the `introAction` section |
| **Orbit rings** | Transition and motion markers |

### Typography Style

- EN display: uppercase, wide tracking, bold or regular weight
- KR body: medium/regular, sentence case
- Mixing EN headers with KR body is intentional — it is part of the brand voice, not a compromise

---

## Tone of Voice

### Principles

| Tone | Description |
|---|---|
| **Bold** | We don't hedge. "We design" not "we try to design." Confidence is the default register. |
| **Experimental** | Willing to try sentence structures, punctuation, or framing that surprises — but always in service of clarity. |
| **Precise** | Every word earns its place. No filler copy. If a sentence can be cut and the meaning survives, cut it. |
| **Warm at scale** | We are a small team that handles serious brands — intimate in conversation, confident in scope. |
| **Mission-language** | Borrow from aerospace: launch, orbit, mission, trajectory, control, signal. Use purposefully — never more than the content warrants. |

### English Copy Style

- Display headlines: title-case or ALL CAPS, 3–7 words preferred
- Subheadlines: sentence case, conversational
- Body: short paragraphs (2–3 lines), no complex clauses
- CTAs: verb-first, journey-anchored — "Start Your Journey", "Join The Mission", "Let's Launch"

### Korean Copy Style

- 존댓말(formal polite) for all public-facing copy
- Avoid corporate stiffness — write as a creative partner, not a firm
- Short sentences. Line breaks are intentional pacing, not overflow.
- Key phrases: `함께`, `여정`, `브랜드`, `설계`, `경험`
- Avoid: `솔루션`, `최고의`, `최적의`, `고객님` — too transactional, too generic

### What Bad Copy Looks Like Here

These are active anti-patterns. If you write any of these, rewrite.

| ❌ Don't write | ✅ Write instead |
|---|---|
| "우리는 최고의 웹 경험을 제공합니다" | "우리가 만든 웹은 사용자가 스크롤을 멈추게 합니다" |
| "Innovative digital solutions" | "Scroll-triggered 3D brand story, built in Three.js" |
| "We are passionate about design" | "We ship design systems that work across 5 touchpoints" |
| "We use cutting-edge technology" | "Three.js, GSAP, and TypeScript — embedded in the site you actually ship" |
| "브랜드의 가치를 높여드립니다" | "브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있을 때, 설계가 끝난 겁니다" |

### Web Agency Copy Rules

- **Talk about results, not tools.** "Users feel it" not "We use Three.js."
- **Frame process as journey language.** "From brief to launch" not "from start to finish."
- **Every space metaphor must land on a web outcome.** If it doesn't, remove the metaphor.

---

## Homepage Section Copy Reference

The homepage tells a story in sequence. Every section must reinforce the arc: web agency that builds immersive digital experiences, together with clients.

| # | Section | Purpose | EN Reference Copy | KR Reference Copy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Intro** | First contact. The invitation. | "Every great brand needs a launch pad." | "모든 브랜드에는 출발점이 있습니다." |
| 2 | **introAction** | The launch sequence. Mission Control activates. | "We're your Mission Control." | "우리가 그 신호를 받습니다." |
| 3 | **Hero** | The slogan lands. We're in the journey now. | "JOIN THE JOURNEY" | "함께 여정을 씁니다" |
| 4 | **Story** | Why we exist. Our design philosophy. | "We don't decorate. We engineer." | "꾸미는 게 아닙니다. 설계합니다." |
| 5 | **Who** | Our role in the client's story. | "You lead. We build the vessel." | "당신의 브랜드가 주인공입니다. 우리는 그 무대를 만듭니다." |
| 6 | **Why (Skills)** | The proof. Tech stack as credibility. | "This is how we prove it." | "우리가 만드는 방식입니다." |
| 7 | **Services** | What we actually build. Concrete. | "What we ship." | "우리가 만드는 것들" |
| 8 | **Portfolio** | Evidence. Real work. | "Work that became real." | "우리가 함께 만든 결과입니다." |
| 9 | **Partners** | Who has already trusted the journey. | "Brands that joined the journey." | "함께 여정을 걸어온 브랜드들" |
| 10 | **Contact** | The door is open. | "Your journey starts here." | "지금, 여정을 시작하세요." |

- **Every section must make it clear we build digital products** — the space narrative is atmosphere, not the headline

- Section titles must be able to stand alone as brand statements

Active guardrails. If a content direction drifts toward any of these, correct course.

|---|---|
| Aerospace or aviation company | Web agency with a space-as-metaphor brand |
| Abstract art studio with no service clarity | Immersive web studio with defined deliverables |

| "We do everything for you" positioning | "We journey together" partnership positioning |
| A space-themed portfolio site | A web agency that uses space as its storytelling language |
| An agency that lists services without narrative | A partner that walks the full arc from brief to launch to orbit |

---

## Glossary

| Term | Usage |
|---|---|
| **NX-2** | The destination — a metaphor for the client's unrealized brand potential. Not a product name. |
